name: A studio full of small agents, each quietly handling one thing
object: dots, always-on background agents, each represented as a small colored character icon, that watch a specific job (meeting notes, competitor moves, product metrics) and report in on their own
audience: operators and teams who want ongoing monitoring and busywork handled continuously, without having to ask every time
message: This video tells busy teams that dots are not one assistant you prompt, they are many small always-on agents, each one quietly owning a single job and surfacing what matters on its own.

moments.what: a title card reads "dots"; a stylish studio-like office introduces a wall of small colorful character icons, each a distinct dots agent with its own look
two colleagues walk the halls as a wall-mounted screen shows one dots character has already caught a mistake and mapped out the fix on its own, without being asked
moments.copy: I caught the typo already, and I've mapped out the changes.

moments.what: more screens show different dots agents at work in parallel, one tracking edits across meeting notes, one watching for a competitor's move, one flagging a product check before a deadline, while the colleagues glance at phones and wall panels as updates roll in
the pair steps outside into a courtyard as the agents keep working behind them; the film closes on the OpenAI mark
moments.copy: dots, always-on agents built to handle everything.

cta: "dots, always-on agents built to handle everything", delivered as the closing line over the OpenAI mark
why: Giving each background job its own small character, instead of one generic assistant, makes the idea of many parallel always-on agents feel concrete and almost like a team you already know, rather than an abstract automation pitch.
